title: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances
focus: Explain Bayes' rule with a diagnostic test: prior prevalence, sensitivity and false-positive rate give the probability of having the condition after a positive result. Let the learner change all three. Show the four joint probabilities and the posterior. Check that a test with sensitivity equal to the false-positive rate leaves the prior unchanged and that the posterior is 1 when the false-positive rate is 0 (and sensitivity > 0).
audience: first-year engineering students with no statistics background
